review_output: {"summary":"I found no BLOCKER. These are internal helpers, not finished HTTP authorization, and I reviewed them that way. The no-proof path works as stated: the proof is created first but returned only after the insert succeeds inside the transaction, so a failed insert or commit returns nothing. Scope binding is solid: the HMAC covers all three IDs (vendor, live, version), the signature and base64url encoding must be exact, and the visitor row is locked and must match the scope. Revisits are gated by the version's current collectionEnabled and expiry checks, and proof lifetime is capped at issuance by the earlier of the trusted context expiry and the version expiry. The real issues are about lifetime and how failures are reported. Every way verification can fail produces the same error, so a later HTTP layer can't tell an honestly expired proof (or one signed with an old key) from a forged one. It must either lock that browser out or quietly give it a new identity, and a new identity is exactly the visit inflation this design is meant to prevent. Other issues: a revisit returns the old proof, whose expiry can be later than the scope's current effective lifetime, and no expiry is given back to the caller. The provisioning query never sets the database timezone, even though the database guard pins it to UTC. Database rejections come through as raw Prisma errors. There is no key-identifier or key-rotation support. Some smaller maintainability and test-precision issues are also listed.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"Correctness / lifetime semantics / data quality","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visitor-proof.ts, src/lib/live-metric-visitor.ts","issue":"verify() returns the same null for every failure, and provisionMetricVisitor turns all of them into one error, 'Metric visitor proof unavailable'. That covers a validly signed but expired proof, a proof signed with an old key, a clock-skew rejection (issuedAtMs > nowMs) and a forged or tampered proof alike. The primitive offers no supported way to safely replace an honestly expired proof.","evidence":"verify(): `if (value.issuedAtMs > nowMs || value.expiresAtMs <= nowMs ...) return null;` comes after the signature check, but it returns the same null as the earlier signature-mismatch branches. The provisioner does `if (!visitorId || ...) throw new Error(\"Metric visitor proof unavailable\")`. The test case `proofs.issue(scope, 0, 1000).proof` (an expired but authentic proof) expects the same 'proof unavailable' error as `\"forged\"`. A proof's expiresAtMs can be min(context.expiresAt, version.expiresAt). If the trusted context later gets a later expiry (renewed or extended content), the version is still collecting but the browser's proof has expired permanently.","impact":"A future HTTP caller has two choices, both bad: (a) treat every failure as fatal, so a legitimate browser is locked out until it clears the cookie, which then rotates its identity anyway; or (b) clear the cookie and reprovision on any failure, which brings back forged/replayed-proof identity rotation and inflated visit counts. Either way the 'invalid proof must not silently rotate identities' rule can't be enforced precisely. Rotating the key or moving the DB clock backward (for example a failover onto a node whose clock is behind) causes the same mass lockout or rotation.","recommended_fix":"Return a discriminated result from verify, e.g. {ok:true, visitorId, expiresAtMs} | {ok:false, reason:'malformed'|'signature'|'scope'|'expired'|'not_yet_valid'}, and give only a signature-valid, scope-matching proof the 'expired' reason. In the provisioner, raise typed errors (a code field or error classes) so the HTTP layer can apply a written policy, e.g. allow a fresh identity only for an authentic expired proof within the same scope, and add a small clock-skew tolerance for issuedAtMs.","required_test":"Proof unit test: an authentic expired proof gives reason 'expired', and tampered, wrong-key and foreign-scope proofs give distinct non-expired reasons. Provisioner test: an expired authentic proof raises the typed 'expired' error while a forged proof raises 'invalid', and neither writes a row. PG suite: issue a proof under a short context expiry, extend the context, and assert the documented outcome (reprovision or a typed rejection).","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Lifetime semantics","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visitor.ts","issue":"A revisit returns the original proof unchanged, and its embedded expiresAtMs can be later than the current effective lifetime min(context.expiresAt, version.expiresAt), for example after the version expiry or content lease is shortened. Neither issue() nor the revisit path returns an expiry value, so a caller setting cookie Max-Age has to decode the proof itself or guess.","evidence":"On revisit: `return { visitorId, proof: existingProof, created: false };` The locally computed `expiresAtMs` is used only for the `<= nowMs` gate and is never compared with the proof's own expiry. issue() returns `{ visitorId, proof }` with no expiresAtMs. The unit test 'caps proof lifetime at the version' covers only issuance.","impact":"The invariant 'proof lifetime is capped at the version' holds only at issuance. A cookie built from the proof or the original lifetime can outlive the scope. Per-request gating still fails closed, but the stored data and cookie lifetimes drift from the scope's actual lifetime, and every caller has to re-derive the expiry.","recommended_fix":"Return `expiresAt: new Date(Math.min(proofExpiresAtMs, expiresAtMs))` on both paths, have verify return the payload's expiresAtMs, and document that this effective expiry, not the embedded one, controls the cookie lifetime.","required_test":"Issue a proof with expiry 1500, then revisit with version.expiresAt=1200 and nowAt=1000. Assert that the result exposes an effective expiry of 1200 and that no write occurs. On the first visit, assert that the returned expiry equals min(context, version).","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Correctness / time handling","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visitor.ts","issue":"The provisioning query compares version timestamps with clock_timestamp() without pinning the session timezone, while the DB guard explicitly runs with `SET timezone = 'UTC'`. If the columns are Prisma's default `timestamp(3)` without a time zone, the comparison casts them using whatever timezone the session happens to have. The bound `${version.nowAt}` parameter is also converted according to the session timezone.","evidence":"The trigger function declares `SET timezone = 'UTC'`, but the provisioner only runs `SELECT set_config('statement_timeout','5000',true)`. Its filter is `\"collectionStartedAt\"<=clock_timestamp() AND \"expiresAt\">clock_timestamp()`. The revisit path has no trigger behind it, so on revisits this filter is the only start gate.","impact":"With a non-UTC session timezone, the collectionStartedAt gate on revisits shifts by the UTC offset: east of UTC it can accept revisits before collection starts, and west of UTC it rejects valid ones. The JS check `expiresAtMs <= nowMs` catches the expiry side, but the gates no longer match the guard, and failures come back as confusing trigger 23514 errors.","recommended_fix":"Add `SELECT set_config('TimeZone','UTC',true)` alongside the statement_timeout, or confirm the columns are timestamptz and add a migration test that checks this. Cast bound values explicitly, e.g. `${version.nowAt}::timestamptz`.","required_test":"PG test that runs the provisioner with the session `SET TimeZone='Asia/Tokyo'` and again with 'America/Los_Angeles'. Assert that revisits before collectionStartedAt are rejected, revisits after it are accepted, and the stored firstVisitedAt equals the DB instant.","confidence":0.45},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Maintainability / error contract","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visitor.ts","issue":"Failures are plain Error objects distinguished only by message text. Database rejections such as trigger 23514 (expiry or disable racing between the SELECT and the INSERT, or the floor/start boundary), primary-key collisions, statement_timeout and transaction timeout come through as raw Prisma errors. Those errors carry SQL/constraint details and no stable category.","evidence":"`throw new Error(\"Metric visitor scope unavailable\")` is used both for a missing version and for a missing visitor row. The tests match substrings: `rejects.toThrow(\"scope unavailable\")`. The trigger can still raise 'metric visitor collection disabled or outside lifetime' after the provisioner's own check has passed, because the trigger re-checks `v.\"expiresAt\">clock_timestamp()` at insert time.","impact":"The future HTTP layer will need to string-match messages and may leak DB error details or map races to 500s. 'Deleted visitor' and 'collection disabled' can't be told apart for metrics or for client policy.","recommended_fix":"Define a MetricVisitorError with codes (SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE, VISITOR_MISSING, PROOF_INVALID, PROOF_EXPIRED, LIFETIME_UNAVAILABLE). Map Prisma errors with code P2010, Postgres 23514, or a statement-timeout code to those codes, and pass everything else through as an internal error without its message.","required_test":"Unit test: mock $executeRaw rejecting with a Prisma 23514 error and assert the mapped code. PG test: expire the version between the SELECT and the INSERT (using an advisory lock or a short expiresAt) and assert the typed error, with no row and no proof.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"Auth / key management","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visitor-proof.ts","issue":"Proofs have no key identifier and the service accepts only one key, so there is no way to rotate keys gradually. Combined with the policy that an invalid proof is rejected rather than reissued, any key rotation or suspected leak turns every outstanding proof into a hard failure at once.","evidence":"`createMetricVisitorProofService(key: Uint8Array)` signs with a single `secret`. The proof format is `${body}.${sig}` with no version or key ID; the purpose string carries 'v1' but it isn't checked separately.","impact":"Rotating the key, which a leak would require, either locks out or re-identifies all browsers in every live scope at the same moment, causing an availability problem and a data discontinuity.","recommended_fix":"Add a `kid` to the payload or as a prefix, accept {current, previous[]} keys for verification and sign only with current. Have verify report which key matched so the caller can decide whether to reissue.","required_test":"A proof signed with the previous key still verifies after rotation, and a proof whose kid is unknown is rejected with a distinct reason.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"NIT","area":"Data quality / maintainability","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visitor.ts","issue":"browserHash is a deterministic SHA-256 of (scope, visitorId), where visitorId is already the random primary key and is readable in the unencrypted proof body. It carries no information of its own and cannot deduplicate anything.","evidence":"`createHash(\"sha256\").update(JSON.stringify([vendorId, liveId, versionId, issued.visitorId]))`","impact":"Anyone reading a column called browserHash may assume it supports per-browser deduplication. Unique-visitor counts are really just counts of proof issuances, and this is easy to misread in analytics.","recommended_fix":"Document that the column has a 1:1 relationship with id, or compute it with a keyed HMAC if it has to be non-derivable. Name or document it so analytics don't treat it as browser deduplication.","required_test":"A unit test asserting that browserHash is derived only from the scope and visitorId, plus a documentation or analytics test.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"NIT","area":"Maintainability / tests","file":"src/lib/live-metric-visitor.ts, src/lib/live-metric-visitor.test.ts","issue":"The `typeof existingProof !== \"string\"` check after verify() can never be true, because verify already returns null for non-strings. The unit tests rely on the order of mockResolvedValueOnce calls and never assert the isolation level, the timeouts, the FOR SHARE / FOR KEY SHARE clauses or the scope predicates. All four parameterized invalid-proof cases share one test name.","evidence":"`if (!visitorId || typeof existingProof !== \"string\")`. database() chains four mockResolvedValueOnce calls. `it.each([...])(\"rejects invalid proof without a new identity\", ...)` has no %s or %# in the name.","impact":"Small refactors, such as dropping a lock query or changing the isolation level, would still pass the unit tests. Only the external PG suite catches them, and test failures are hard to attribute.","recommended_fix":"Keep the typeof check only as a type narrowing and comment it as such. Assert `$transaction.mock.calls[0][1]` equals {isolationLevel: ReadCommitted, timeout: 10000, maxWait: 5000}, and assert the SQL text contains 'FOR SHARE' / 'FOR KEY SHARE' and binds all three scope IDs. Add %# to the each-test names.","required_test":"Add assertions on the transaction options and the SQL strings and values in the existing unit tests.","confidence":0.5}]}
